title: Founding Pabrai Investment Funds with the Buffett partnership structure
statement: Pabrai copied Warren Buffett's original 1950s partnership fee structure — no management fee, 6% hurdle, 25% of gains above it — to align himself with a small number of partners.
outcome: The structure attracted permanent capital and his funds compounded at roughly 18% annually over their first 15 years, among the best records of the era.

title: Buying Stewart Information Services during the 2008 crisis
statement: With title insurers priced for permanent collapse, Pabrai researched the century of Stewart's cash generation through real-estate cycles and bought heavily as the sector traded near liquidation values.
outcome: Stewart recovered and multiplied from his purchase prices; Pabrai called it a canonical 'heads I win big, tails I don't lose much' position.

title: The Dhando Investor — articulating low-risk high-uncertainty buying
statement: Pabrai systematized his method as 'Dhando' — the Indian word for business done with margin of safety — arguing that the best investments are low-risk bets on high-uncertainty situations the market prices as high-risk.
outcome: The book became a modern value-investing staple and popularized asymmetric-payoff thinking among retail investors.

title: The 2011 CRM misstep and its public postmortem
statement: Pabrai bought into salesforce.com-style high-flying software names after being drawn in by growth narratives — a violation of his own framework, which he dissected publicly at subsequent shareholder meetings.
outcome: He sold at a loss and published the analysis as a teaching case; his annual meeting 'mistakes' sessions became a celebrated transparency practice.

title: Copying — the explicit adoption of others' proven frameworks
statement: Pabrai openly articulated his belief that originality is overrated in investing: identify the best systems — Buffett's partnership, Kelly sizing, checklist investing — and copy them shamelessly.
outcome: The 'shameless cloning' doctrine, including tracking other great investors' purchases, became his signature contribution to value-investing pedagogy.

title: Dakshana Foundation — funding gifted poor students at scale
statement: Pabrai and his wife committed to giving a majority of their wealth, founding Dakshana to coach academically gifted but impoverished Indian students for the IIT entrance examination.
outcome: Dakshana has placed thousands of students into the IITs and other top institutions, with alumni entering India's engineering elite; the Pabrais signed the Giving Pledge in 2019.
